anomalies.observed: The isolated secondary-side I2C lines of the pH bridge (U2 SDA1/SCL1, sheet 1 'I2C Sensors', labelled NET0007/NET0008) and the EC bridge (U1 SDA1/SCL1, labelled NET0005/NET0006) carry the same net names as primary-domain ESP32 GPIOs and actuator lines: NET0007 also appears on M2A IO10 and on the main-pump gate resistor R14 (->T1 gate); NET0008 on M2A IO11; NET0005 on M2A IO8/ADC8/LED and on the pH-pump STEP pin U8.16.
anomalies.expected: Spec §4.2: 'U3 (pH) and U4 (EC) each present a secondary isolated I2C pair (/SDA_pH/SCL_pH, /SDA_EC/SCL_EC) that connects directly to M2 (EZO-pH) and M3 (EZO-EC) respectively, each with its own isolated supply/ground domain generated on-chip.' anomalies.impact: The 2.5 kV galvanic isolation of the wet pH/EC channels is defeated: the probe I2C lines are tied to the main-pump gate drive and the dosing STEP/LED GPIOs, causing bus contention, loss of pH/EC communication, and possible damage to the probes or isolators.

anomalies.observed: On sheet 1 'POWER TRAIN' the buck U6 (TPS62933) RT oscillator-timing pin (pin 1, with R41 21k to GND) is labelled NET0056, which is the same net name used on the STDBY pins of all three TMC2209 drivers (U8.20, U9.20, U5.20, sheet 2) and on ESP32 IO19.
anomalies.expected: Spec §3 lists RT as a dedicated timing net ('/RT_BK') connected only to its frequency-setting resistor; STDBY is a separate digital control net driven by a GPIO.
anomalies.impact: Loading the analog RT pin with the digital standby line and a GPIO corrupts the buck's switching frequency (unstable/incorrect +5V rail) and makes the motor-driver standby control behave unpredictably.
